statement: Abd al-Rahman III of the Umayyad Emirate of Córdoba proclaimed himself Caliph in 929 — a direct challenge to the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad and the Fatimid Caliphate in Tunisia. The proclamation was a response to Fatimid pressure on Spain's North African trade and represented the peak of Umayyad power in al-Andalus. The Caliphate of Córdoba (929–1031) coincided with the apex of Moorish learning and art (the Great Mosque expansion, the palace-city of Medina Azahara). The caliphate collapsed in the chaos of the Fitna (1009–1031), fragmenting into the Taifa kingdoms.
